results.title: Polylane: AI agents that fix issues before they become incidents | Product Hunt
results.content:
What do you think? …

Hey Product Hunt, Matanya here, co-founder of Polylane.Hard incidents usually come with several plausible causes. Was it the last deploy, the database, the edge, or something else?With Polylane Swarms, agents investigate those leads in parallel and share their evidence on one board. Another agent has to reproduce the evidence before a finding is confirmed. The lead brings the confirmed findings together into the cause and a proposed fix.The swarm can add agents as new leads appear, up to 25 including the lead. You can follow each agent and the board from the thread sidebar.To try it, connect GitHub, start a thread and choose Swarm. It's available on paid plans.What incident would you put a swarm on? We'd love to hear how it works on your stack. [...] As a solo dev, on-call is just me, so a swarm doing the parallel digging is pretty appealing — I'm usually the one jumping between the last deploy, the database, and the logs trying to figure out which one it was. The shared evidence board is the part that caught my eye. Does the memory carry across incidents, so the next time the same kind of thing breaks it already knows where to look first?

@jcbuilds we actually build an ongoing log of everything happening in your infrastructure and add events every day, so we always know what happened before and if we're seeing it again [...] congrats on the launch matanya. i would put it on the day signups drop and nobody knows if its tracking, a deploy or the ads. usually 3 people check 3 places and argue in slack for hours. can i tell the swarm which leads are already ruled out so it doesnt burn agents on them?

Having a second agent reproduce the evidence before a cause counts is the part that would stop the wild goose chase I usually get at two in the morning, because the first plausible answer is rarely the real one. When two agents disagree, does the swarm pick a side or keep both open until someone tests them?

Title: Polylane: AI agents that fix issues before they become incidents | Product Hunt
## AI agents that fix issues before they become incidents. Polylane connects your code, infra and observability data, investigates every issue and opens a pull request with the fix. This is the 4th launch from Polylane. ## Polylane for Cloudflare. An AI on-call engineer for your Cloudflare apps. Polylane catches issues across your Cloudflare apps, follows the connections between Workers, databases, queues and storage, and investigates the root cause using your code, logs and recent changes. When the fix is in your code, it opens a pull request for review. Connect with one read-only Cloudflare token. ArticosTest your messaging on your audience, right inside Claude or ChatGPT. Polylane Impact AnalysisCatch risky pull requests before they break production. Launched on October 15th, 2026. Polylane for VercelAn AI on-call engineer for your Vercel apps. PolylaneAI agents that fix production before you wake up. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Polylane. Polylane is built on Cloudflare. We use Workers, D1, Workflows, Durable Objects, Queues, R2… a lot of Cloudflare. That flexibility is a big part of how we’re able to build Polylane. The database it talks to? Polylane for Cloudflare connects those pieces, investigates what’s going wrong, and opens a pull request when the fix is in your code. We use it heavily to build and run Polylane itself. It helps us ship hundreds of PRs a week safely, and we’ve put a lot of work into making it useful for our own team. We hope it’s as useful for you as it is for us. Give it a try, and let us know what you think. I run a couple of Workers and D1 apps, and the incident I worry about most isn't in the code. It's a deploy that ships code expecting a column before the D1 migration that adds it has been applied. Does Polylane compare the Worker's code with the migrations actually applied to the database, and say "apply migration 0007" when that's the fix, rather than opening a PR? Also, the single read-only token is the right default for anything that reads production. Read-only access is the only sensible way to hand off monitoring.
